question: An observer at the top of a tower observes that two cars are running towards the foot of the tower at a distance of 120 m from each other making angles of depression α and β such that α > β and tan α = sqrt3 and tan β = (1)/(sqrt3). Find the height of the tower.
solution:
**Given:** 

Two cars are running towards the foot of the tower at a distance of 120 m from each other

Angles of depression α and β such that α > β 

tan α = sqrt{3} and tan β = (1)/(sqrt{3)}

**Concept used:**

tanθ = (Perpendicular)/(Base) =( P)/(B)

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17ad81c926a90b9dd8cb9bdc87ef75ba823145e6318601a64a93b55c57d96c7a.png] 

In Triangle CBD,

tanα = (CB)/(DB) = (h)/(x)

⇒ sqrt{3} =( h)/(x)

⇒ x = (h)/(sqrt{3)} 

Again in Triangle ABC,

tanβ = (CB)/(AB )= (h)/((120 + x))

⇒ 1/√3 = h/[120 + (h/√3)]

⇒ 1/√3 = h√3/[120√3 + h]

⇒ 120√3 + h = (√3)(√3)h

⇒ 120√3 + h = 3h

⇒ 120√3 = 2h

⇒ h = (120√3)/2 = 60√3 m

**∴ The height of the tower is 60√3 m.**
